doesTheMapBreak: No. The map renders the static hillshade under the online tiles, the site markers, the region outlines and the pole marker. With no manifest the map reports the static hillshade as unavailable and falls back to the vector layers over a plain background, as tests/basemap.test.ts checks.
imageExtentM: The image covers the raster's true extent, +/- 304,000 m (80S to the pole, 7600 x 7600 px at 80 m). An earlier manifest wrote +/- 457,440 m, the Moon Trek layer's extent (75S); corrected 2026-11-15, with the header read from the project's own checkHeader on the 80 m DEM (origin -304000, 304000; resolution 80 m).
tests: 12 passed across tests/basemap.test.ts, including that no manifest is read as availability and that a manifest claiming a synthetic surface is rejected
verdict: The static hillshade is built and shipped: south-pole-hillshade.png (2,948,250 bytes, 1900 x 1900, 320 m per pixel) and basemap.json sit under app/public/data/basemap/, drawn from the LOLA 80 m hillshade raster (LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ_HILL.TIF) by npm run build:basemap on 2026-11-15. The app loads and validates the manifest, and the map draws the picture under the Moon Trek tiles as an image layer at the raster's true extent; the tiles cover it while they load, so it is the picture you see when the tiles fail.
whatBuiltIt: LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ_HILL.TIF from the LOLA product page, placed in data/, then npm run build:basemap. The builder downsamples to at most 2048 px, tags the manifest as LOLA shaded relief, records the product, source, build date and command, and the app refuses to show any image whose manifest lacks those.
